name: Banks
stance_summary: Maintain Stage 1 OW (~69.9): credit demand supported by domestic activity; prefer scaled franchises with funding and risk-management advantages over homogeneous lender beta.
overview: Large diversified banks retain liability and distribution advantages that matter more when policy is neutral and deposit pricing is competitive.
Asset quality and unsecured books are stock-specific; treat sector OW as a franchise-quality call, not a blanket financials long.
PSU scale (notably SBI and selected large PSUs) can complement private leaders when liability franchise and capital are intact.
The investable universe is widened to ~18 names; the Stage 2 shortlist concentrates on ten higher-conviction franchises and selected challengers.
Stage 1 thesis stands: deposit pricing, asset quality and margin discipline dominate a simple rate-cut narrative.

sub_themes.title: Large private franchises
sub_themes.summary: HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank anchor private-sector quality via funding mix, distribution and risk systems.

sub_themes.title: PSU liability scale
sub_themes.summary: SBI and selected large PSUs offer deposit franchise scale; cyclical mid-tier PSUs stay in the universe, not the core shortlist.

sub_themes.title: Deposit competition and margins
sub_themes.summary: Neutral policy raises the importance of CASA quality and pricing discipline versus wholesale-funded growth.

sub_themes.title: Improving private and SFB challengers
sub_themes.summary: Federal, IDFC First and AU offer incremental upside if liability and underwriting trajectories continue to improve.

sub_themes.title: Asset quality and unsecured watchpoints
sub_themes.summary: Unsecured or concentrated stress can re-rate names quickly even when sector NPAs look benign in aggregate.

drivers: Broad-based credit demand from domestic activity
Franchise advantages in deposits and distribution for scaled leaders
Improving mid-tier challengers where liability and underwriting are visibly strengthening
risks: Unsecured or SME stress lifting credit costs
Governance or underwriting setbacks at individual banks
Policy or liquidity surprises that reprice funding costs

positive: Credit costs stay benign while growth remains broad-based
Street may under-differentiate franchise quality within a wider bank universe
negative: Deposit competition or unsecured stress weakens margins and asset quality faster than consensus models
Homogeneous 'banks OW' ignores stock-specific liability and risk books

shortlist.name: HDFC Bank
thesis: Core private-sector expression of scaled funding, distribution and risk architecture.
Best used as the primary OW vehicle when deposit competition is elevated.
why_now: Stage 1 prefers scaled franchises over undifferentiated lender beta.
key_risks: Margin pressure from deposit repricing
Integration and growth-mix execution remain watchpoints

shortlist.name: ICICI Bank
shortlist.role_in_sector: Large private franchise / risk culture compounder
thesis: Second core private holding with strong retail/SME franchise and improved risk culture versus prior cycles.
Complements HDFC Bank without relying on PSU beta.
why_now: Useful co-leader when expressing Banks OW through private quality.
key_risks: Competitive intensity in retail unsecured
Market-sensitive fee and treasury income swings

shortlist.name: State Bank of India
thesis: Distinctive deposit franchise and balance-sheet scale among Indian banks.
Complements private leaders when capital and credit mix remain constructive.
why_now: Provides PSU scale exposure without making cyclical mid-tier PSUs the core OW expression.
key_risks: Policy and credit-mix interventions
Operating leverage and cost ratios versus private peers

shortlist.name: Kotak Mahindra Bank
thesis: Quality compounder profile with historically conservative underwriting culture.
Useful satellite to the two large private leaders.
why_now: Fits preference for franchise quality when deposit competition is elevated.
key_risks: Growth versus peer share-of-wallet
Leadership and strategy continuity perceptions

shortlist.name: Axis Bank
thesis: Large private challenger with improving franchise trajectory versus prior cycles.
Offers incremental upside versus leaders if liability and credit outcomes continue to stabilize.
why_now: Diversifies the shortlist beyond the top-two private names without moving into high-risk mid-tiers.
key_risks: Still more sensitive to credit and liability setbacks than the top franchises
Competitive intensity in retail and corporate books

shortlist.name: Bank of Baroda
thesis: Large PSU with meaningful liability scale and a cleaner recovery narrative than weaker mid-tiers.
Secondary PSU expression beside SBI rather than a homogeneous PSU basket.
why_now: Adds PSU diversification inside the shortlist without relying on smaller cyclical names.
key_risks: Credit-mix and policy sensitivity
Deposit cost and operating efficiency versus private peers

shortlist.name: Federal Bank
thesis: Private mid-tier franchise with a visible growth and liability-build narrative.
Useful challenger sleeve when leaders are fully valued on franchise quality.
why_now: Broadens the shortlist into improving private mid-tiers without high-risk classifications.
key_risks: Scale disadvantage versus large private banks
Asset-quality sensitivity in faster growth phases

shortlist.name: IDFC First Bank
thesis: Liability transformation and retailisation story remains the core investment debate.
Higher-beta private expression than Federal within the challenger sleeve.
why_now: Fits Stage 1 preference for improving challengers with clear franchise-build agendas.
key_risks: Funding cost and deposit franchise still the swing factor
Credit costs can surprise during growth bursts

shortlist.name: AU Small Finance Bank
thesis: Leading SFB franchise with retail/MSME orientation and growth optionality.
Complements scheduled commercial bank names with a different liability and product mix.
why_now: Extends the shortlist into SFB quality without diluting into high-risk microfinance-heavy names.
key_risks: Funding and regulatory transition risks as an SFB
Credit cycle sensitivity in retail/MSME books

shortlist.name: IndusInd Bank
thesis: Large private bank where franchise repair and governance outcomes dominate the thesis.
Included as a monitored turnaround sleeve, not a core quality compounder.
why_now: Completes the ten-name shortlist with an explicit turnaround risk/reward profile.
key_risks: Execution and credibility of the turnaround
Asset-quality and liability surprises can re-rate quickly

methodology_notes: KPI values are intentionally null in this pack; qualitative badges are research judgment, not audited financial metrics.
No NIM, GNPA or credit-cost percentages were verified from filings for this release — use Data unavailable from reliable sources. until cited.
Shortlist is a ten-name preference ranking within an eighteen-name Stage 1 Banks universe — not portfolio weights.
Universe-only names (including newly added PSUs and mid-tiers) appear on the Companies page without authored shortlist notes.
Returns and prices are joined from companies.by_sector.banks at render time.
